_roadWidth: 54.6, TAKEN FROM tools/level3_geometry.json and confirmed against the plate rather than assumed. check_level3.py re-derives it by casting normals off each lane's centreline through the painted track and taking the NARROWEST lane's median, which reads 55.0 -- 0.7% out. The narrowest lane is the honest number for the same reason it was on level 2: the road has to fit its tightest stretch. Measured lane by lane the shared tail reads about 65, because the track there runs alongside painted field markings and a pale apron that no colour test can separate from the track itself; that is a limit of the measurement, not a wider road.
note: SPORTS COMPLEX AT DUSK, and the first level with a fork. Every coordinate here comes from tools/level3_geometry.json, which arrived with the plate: two branch centrelines, a shared tail, the merge point, the road width and fifteen pads. Nothing in this file was traced or typed by hand. Re-check it with `python3 tools/check_level3.py`, which re-derives the road width and both branch lengths off the painted plate and fails if they disagree with the geometry file by more than 3%. TWO THINGS WERE COMPUTED RATHER THAN COPIED, and both are stated in their own notes below: the off-plate gateway points at each end, and the snap of each branch's last waypoint onto the merge point.
_heroStart: MEASURED, not eyeballed, by the same rule level 2 uses: his whole 120x55 footprint must be clear of anything that is not open turf, and then the clearances are maximised. This spot is 97.3 px from the painted road's EDGE (level 2's is 94.2), 80.1 px from the nearest pad (level 2's is 84.5) and 100% turf under every pixel of the footprint. He is about 120 world px tall and this is his FEET, so his head sits at y=424 -- well inside the board. IT IS ALSO THE NEAREST LEGAL SPOT TO THE MERGE, 166 px from it. On a fork that is where a hero is worth most: he covers whatever came down either branch instead of guessing a side. The player can rally him elsewhere; this is only where he starts.
_spotRadius: 34, level 1's and level 2's. Two pads need 2 x spotRadius between centres before their tap targets overlap, so 34 needs 68 and the closest pair here is 74.0 -- pads 5 and 10, and again 8 and 14. It clears by 6. As on level 2 the radius is NOT the adjustable end of this: world 1280 renders to 844 CSS px, so 34 world px is a 44.8 px tap diameter and anything under 44 pt is smaller than a thumb.
_waypoints: THE SHARED TAIL, which is the trunk every enemy finishes on. It is `shared` from the geometry file with two edits, neither of them a coordinate change: its first point is set to the merge point exactly (they already agree to 0.00 px, so this is a no-op that documents intent), and one gateway point is appended at x=1340 so enemies walk off the plate rather than vanishing at its edge. That last point is NOT traced -- it is a new point on the line the tail is already travelling as it reaches the edge, which is how level 2 does it and for the reason level 2 records: dragging the final traced point out instead would swing the closing segment off the paint.
_lanes: TWO GATES, ONE EXIT. Both branches run in from off the left edge and merge into the trunk at its waypoint 0, which is the merge point. A branch ENDS at the join -- that is what the lane engine expects, and each branch's last traced point was 3.26 px (upper) and 8.47 px (lower) short of the declared merge, so both were snapped onto it. Left alone an enemy would have stepped those few pixels sideways as it transferred. THE TWO ROUTES ARE THE SAME LENGTH: 1560.18 and 1560.15 px gate to exit, 0.03 px apart. That is in the geometry, not something arranged here, and it is worth knowing because it means neither gate is the fast one -- a group sent down either branch arrives on the same clock, so a wave that splits across both is a genuine two-front problem rather than a staggered one. The two branches alone are 887.93 and 887.90, and the trunk they share is 672.25.
_buildSpots: FIFTEEN PADS, copied from the geometry file untouched. Every one of them is verified by check_level3.py on three properties the level cannot be played without. IN RANGE: each pad is 90.0 to 114.0 world px from the nearest lane centreline -- measured 91.7 to 112.0 -- against a tower range of 112, so every pad reaches the road it is meant to cover. This is the check level 2 shipped without, and its absence is why level 2 was unwinnable at 0 of 60. APART: the closest pair is 74.0 px, over the 68 that spotRadius needs. ON GROUND: each pad's 24 px core is on open turf -- not the track, the bleachers, a bench, the fence, a goal, the pool, a light pole, a traffic cone or the football. Measured at 98.7% turf in the worst core (pad 9) and 100% in nine of the fifteen, with the remainder scattered single-pixel grass detail rather than any object: nothing survives a 30 px blob filter.
